source: Length in centimeters and meters, mass in grams and kilograms, liquid volume in milliliters and liters, and temperature in degrees. Read the scale at eye level.
Reading a ruler from 1 instead of 0, or reading a measuring cup from above instead of at eye level.
Scientists all over the world use the same units, the metric system, so they can share results. Its units grow by tens, hundreds and thousands, which makes them easy to change.
Line the end of the object up with the 0 mark, not the end of the ruler. This pencil is 7.5 cm long.
Read a liquid at eye level, at the bottom of its curved top. This cylinder holds 40 mL.
Always write the unit. "The table is 2" could mean 2 meters or 2 centimeters, a big difference!
A string is 3 meters long. How many centimeters is that?
Starting at 1 on the ruler, or reading a measuring cup from above. Start at 0, and bend down so your eyes are level with the liquid.
